newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks down in nervous London trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks down in nervous London trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London fell on Wednesday in line with bearish markets in London and New York as overseas concerns fuelled market jitters and sparked aggressive selling, traders said. At 1550 GMT, the Hang Seng London Reference index was down 225.51 points at 12964.09after the Hong Kong Hang Seng closed down 152.86 points at 13,189.60. Dealers reported heavy selling as U.S. data issued Wednesday and worries over more figures due Thursday intensified fears of inflationary pressure in the United States and a possible raising of interest rates.

"There is a lot of profit to be taken at this level," said one dealer. "Why wait until after Christmas?" Another trader said: "With the weakness in U.S. treasuries today, there was only one way the Hang Seng could go." Dealers said market nerves had not been helped by various news stories, including Saudia Arabia's claim it has data proving Iran was behind the June bombing in the U.S.
By 1615 GMT, London's FTSE 100 index was down 54.6 points at 3981.1, while the Dow was down 97.26 points at 6375.99.
